name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,473

clue.text: Rushes to hide son

blocks.note: a pelt is an animal's skin or hide
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off to conceal their boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rushes' reads as the verb of the surface but is the definition, and 'hide' is a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pelt is to move very fast, as in pelting down the road, so pelts means hurries along.

clue.text: Cake made from tip of pale bananas not eaten

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its very first letter, so only that is taken
going bananas is going crazy, so the following words are scrambled

blocks.note: the opening letter of pale
the eight letters of not eaten rearranged

explanation.surface: A cake baked with pale bananas that nobody wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the cake's ingredient but means crazy, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Panettone is a tall Italian sweet bread with dried fruit, eaten at Christmas, a kind of cake.

clue.text: Fabric lining sparkly cradle

indicators.note: a lining sits inside a garment, so the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A glittery cot with a fabric lining.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a trademark stretchy synthetic fibre used in sportswear, so it is a fabric.

clue.text: Fairy and supporters returned to nick

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the combined words are read backwards

blocks.note: an elf is a fairy creature
fans are supporters of a team

explanation.surface: A fairy and her fans went back to the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' suggests a British slang police station; here it is the slang verb meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle is British slang for taking something quickly, often without permission, like to pinch or steal.

clue.text: Communication government intended to announce

indicators.note: announcing is saying something out loud, so the word for intended is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the state is the governing body of a country
intended means meant, which is spoken the same as this ending

explanation.surface: A government's intended message is about to be made public.
explanation.walkthrough: STATE plus a sound-alike of MEANT gives STATEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a formal message or declaration, a kind of communication issued to others.

clue.text: Serbian contracted skin problem from grass

indicators.note: a contracted word is shortened to its first and last letters, as in abbreviations like Dr

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Serbian
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A Serb caught an itchy skin complaint from grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the source of an allergy but is British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass on someone and to snitch both mean informing on them to the police or authorities.

clue.text: Last word by competent subject

blocks.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer
able means capable or competent

explanation.surface: Having the last word belongs to a capable person.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable means liable or open to something, as in 'subject to' a law or influence.

clue.text: Bouncy castle collapsing round setter

indicators.note: a collapsing structure falls into disorder, so these letters fall into a new order
round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the setter

blocks.note: the letters of castle rearranged
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: An inflatable castle deflates around the puzzle's compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncy castle' reads as one thing, but 'Bouncy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic springs back into shape when stretched, so it is springy and bouncy.

clue.text: English row about food close to Spanish city

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the slang word for food is read backwards
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
a din is a loud noise or row
grub is slang for food
the final letter of Spanish

explanation.surface: An English quarrel about food near a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish city' looks like the definition, but Spanish only gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish capital is a specific example of the general category: a large, important urban settlement.

clue.text: Youngsters support partners

blocks.note: a tee supports a golf ball
North and South are partners in bridge

explanation.surface: Young people stand by their partners.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as a pair against East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Teens are people aged thirteen to nineteen, adolescents rather than adults.

clue.text: Sailor in awfully nice surroundings points to fruit

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so these letters come out jumbled
surroundings encircle whatever sits in them, so the sailor goes inside

blocks.note: the letters of nice rearranged
a tar is an old word for a seaman
N and E, two points of the compass

explanation.surface: A sailor in pleasant surroundings is pointed towards some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' suggests directions to the fruit, but it gives two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a common stone fruit.

clue.text: Capulets' second newlywed leaving Romeo in lodge

indicators.note: second points to the letter in second position of the possessive word before it
leaving means departing, so the letter for Romeo goes out of the word for newlywed

blocks.note: the second letter of Capulets
a bride is a woman just married
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Juliet, a Capulet, newly wed, must leave Romeo and stay behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodge' looks like a noun for a building, but here it is the verb meaning reside.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is an old word for dwell or stay somewhere, just as to lodge is to reside.

clue.text: Pictures returned to fellows in charge of illegal trade

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word for pictures is read backwards

blocks.note: pictures are works of art
F is the abbreviation for fellow, doubled for the plural
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Paintings sent back to men who run a black-market business.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic as a noun means dealing in illegal goods, as in drug or arms traffic.

clue.text: Ban site for redevelopment in part of French Riviera

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds something in a new form, so these letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Planners bar a plot from redevelopment on the Côte d'Azur.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibes is a resort town between Cannes and Nice, on the Mediterranean coast of southern France.

clue.text: Shellfish found in broken toys by European river

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, so these letters are put back in another order

blocks.note: the letters of toys rearranged
E is the standard abbreviation for European
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A shellfish turns up among smashed playthings beside a river in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is an edible bivalve mollusc, a kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Waving flags found in prop containing English chart

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the word for prop goes around the other pieces

blocks.note: to shore up is to prop, and a shore is a prop or support
E is the standard abbreviation for English
a chart is a map

explanation.surface: Signal flags discovered in a stage prop wrapped round an English chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prop' looks theatrical, but a shore is a beam that props up a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is signalling by holding two flags in set positions, so it is a system of waving flags.

clue.text: Want king to stop person becoming parliamentary usher

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so these pieces go into the middle of the word for person

blocks.note: bod is informal British for a person
to want is to lack
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch wants to prevent someone being appointed to a ceremonial post.
explanation.walkthrough: Bod is informal British for a person, often used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Black Rod is the official of the House of Lords who summons the Commons at the State Opening of Parliament.

clue.text: Competition in foreign chalet overseen by academic

indicators.note: foreign means strange or alien, so these letters take an unfamiliar order
in a down clue, being overseen means the academic sits above and around, enclosing the jumble

blocks.note: a don is a university lecturer
the letters of chalet rearranged

explanation.surface: A contest held in a chalet abroad, supervised by a professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlon is an athletics contest of ten events, a competition for all-round athletes.

clue.text: Sends out for meals containing cassava root

indicators.note: the root is the starting point, so only the first letter is kept
containing means holding inside, so the word for meals goes around

blocks.note: lunches are midday meals
the opening letter of cassava

explanation.surface: Someone orders out for meals with cassava root in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root' fits the vegetable, but it signals only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch is to send off a ship, rocket or product, so launches means sends out.

clue.text: Chaps at head of table tucking into meal cooked with cheese

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken
cooking changes the form of the ingredients, so these letters are mixed
tucking into something puts you inside it, so the first pieces go within the other

blocks.note: chaps are men
the opening letter of table
the letters of meal rearranged

explanation.surface: Men at the head of the table tuck into a meal made with cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At head of table' sounds like seating, but it only takes the table's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a Swiss hard cheese with large holes, so it is an example of the defining word.

clue.text: Distinguished restaurant fully booked?

blocks.note: first meaning: famous, worthy of note
second meaning, read as two words: what a full restaurant tells you

explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO TABLE, it is a full restaurant's reply; the question mark flags this whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means remarkable or eminent, which is what distinguished means of a person or achievement.

clue.text: Try substantial detailed typeface

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, it means with the tail cut off, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a go is an attempt or try
thick means solid and substantial

explanation.surface: Try out a heavy, intricate font.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like intricate but splits as de-tailed: THICK loses its K.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is a heavy black-letter style of type, so it names a kind of font.

clue.text: Colours of old bits of cooks' equipment?

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a range is a large cooking stove

explanation.surface: The colours of antique kitchen gear.
explanation.walkthrough: A range is a large kitchen stove, such as an Aga.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange is a colour between red and yellow, so oranges are shades of that colour.

clue.text: Series of deposits

blocks.note: first meaning: graded sequences, as of musical notes
second meaning: crusty layers left by hard water in kettles

explanation.walkthrough: 'Series of deposits' sounds like bank payments; the two nouns are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Scales are ordered sequences of notes or grades, and also chalky crusts left by hard water.

clue.text: Device for winding pasta twists into drained corn

indicators.note: twisting something bends it out of shape, so these letters are rearranged
drained means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters
into places one piece inside another

blocks.note: the outer letters of corn
the letters of pasta rearranged

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget that twirls pasta in with sweetcorn after draining it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Device for winding' looks like a pasta fork in the surface, but it is a ship's winch.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a revolving drum on a ship around which rope or cable is wound to haul it.

clue.text: Swear by remedy containing sulphur

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the word for remedy goes around the symbol

blocks.note: a cure is a remedy
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Someone swears by a sulphur-based treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swear by' reads as trust in, but 'by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to use bad language, so it means the same as to swear.

clue.text: Priest in hut finding prayer beads

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for priest inside the word for hut

blocks.note: a chalet is a wooden hut or cabin
P is a dictionary abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: A cleric in a mountain hut discovers a rosary.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a string of beads used for counting prayers, a shorter form of the rosary.

clue.text: Animal stopping gorilla mating

indicators.note: stopping is plugging a gap, so the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A creature interrupting a pair of apes as they breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A llama is a domesticated South American mammal related to the camel.

clue.text: Lozenge recipe at hospital used by old doctor

blocks.note: R, from Latin recipe, heads prescriptions
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
O is the standard abbreviation for old
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine degree

explanation.surface: An elderly doctor prescribes a throat lozenge at the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lozenge' suggests a throat sweet, but here it is the diamond shape. R heads old prescriptions, meaning 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb, or rhombus, is a four-sided figure with equal sides, the diamond shape heraldry calls a lozenge.

clue.text: Vessel found in first part of 'Hope and Glory' translated by first rate lecturer

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
translating changes words into a new form, so these letters are rewritten in a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter of Hope
taken as written, to be mixed with the H
A1 means first rate, written with the letter I for the digit
L is the standard abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A first-class lecturer renders 'Land of Hope and Glory' and finds a sacred cup in it.
explanation.walkthrough: H with GLORY rearranged gives HOLYGR; AI and L finish HOLY GRAIL. A1 is printed AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Grail is the legendary cup or dish used by Christ at the Last Supper, a sacred vessel.

clue.text: Refreshment in reflective bishop's office including seven new loaves for starters

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the number's letters take a fresh order
starters are the opening course, so only the initial letter is used
a reflection shows things back to front, so the office is read backwards
including takes something in, so the office holds the other pieces

blocks.note: a bishop's see is his seat of office
the opening letter of loaves
the letters of seven rearranged

explanation.surface: A reflective bishop takes refreshment in his study, with seven fresh loaves to start.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE backwards is EES, which holds L and EVENS, giving E-LEVENS-ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a light mid-morning snack or drink, a British break taken around eleven o'clock.

clue.text: Rejected eggs containing a flaw

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word for eggs is read backwards
containing means holding inside, so the article goes within

blocks.note: nits are the eggs of lice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eggs are sent back because they hold a defect.
explanation.walkthrough: NITS reversed is STIN, which takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a blemish or mark that spoils something, so it is a defect or flaw.
